news.title: AI tool poisoning exposes a major flaw in enterprise agent security
news.summary_raw: AI agents choose tools from shared registries by matching natural-language descriptions. But no human is verifying whether those descriptions are true. I discovered this gap when I filed Issue #141 in the CoSAI secure-ai-tooling repository. I assumed it would be treated as a single risk entry. The repository maintainer saw it differently and split my submission into two separate issues: One covering selection-time threats (tool impersonation, metadata manipulation); the other covering execution-
news.summary: AI tool poisoning has been found to expose a major flaw in enterprise agent security. This is because AI agents choose tools from shared registries by matching natural-language descriptions, without human verification of those descriptions. This gap in the system was discovered and a related issue filed in the CoSAI secure-ai-tooling repository.
news.enterprise_use: UK SMB IT teams and MSPs should consider updating their AI tool security protocols to include human verification of natural-language descriptions. This can be done by implementing additional checks and balances in their AI tool registries.
